title.narrative: Translating the SDG Framework in BIH into Sustainable and Inclusive Growth, UNDP
Översätta SDG Framework i BIH till hållbar och inkluderande tillväxt, UNDP

description.narrative: Programmet syftar till att stödja regeringarna i BIH i deras ansträngningar att uppnå sina mål för hållbar utveckling som överenskommits i SDG Framework i BIH genom att förbättra styrsystemet, främja smart tillväxt och i slutändan bidra till att skapa ett samhälle med lika möjligheter. Målet kommer att eftersträvas genom tre sammanlänkade och ömsesidigt förstärkande resultat som genomförs på alla nivåer av regeringar i BIH.

The programme aims to supporting the governments in BIH in their efforts to achieve their sustainable development targets agreed in the SDG Framework in BIH by improving the governance system, fostering smart growth, and ultimately contributing to creating society of equal opportunities. The aim will be pursued through three interlinked and mutually reinforcing results implemented across all levels of governments in BIH.

The overall objective of the program aims to contribute to accelerated achievements of Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) through supporting governance systems and private sector engagement towards green, sustainable and inclusive growth.
The Project is based on implementation of two outcomes and respective outputs:
Outcome 1: Authorities at state, entity and Brcko District levels effectively work on planning, implementing, monitoring and reporting on the SDG Framework in BIH as well as fostering development partnerships
Outcome 2: Cantonal and local governments actively contribute to implementation of the SDG Framework in BIH.
In summary, the programme will provide required support to the authorities in Bosnia and Herzegovina in their activities and progress towards the Sustainable Development Goals as per targets defined in the SDG Framework in Bosnia and Herzegovina. Actions will be interlinked and reinforced engaging all levels of government in BIH, relevant for planning, monitoring and reporting. Further, the activities will be coupled with active participation and contribution of the cantonal and local governments and private sector aimed at implementing SDG Framework.

description.narrative:
During the reporting period the Programme successfully supported the SDG Councils effective functioning, including the revision and adoption of an updated SDG indicator list by the Council of Ministers. The national perception survey contributed to data availability for SDG 16, and development of a database by Federal Institute for Development Programming signaled progress in evidence-based decision-making. Further expected outcomes included engagement with key national stakeholders and the integration of SDGs in strategic documents like the United Nation Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework. More specifically, during the reporting period the program supported the work SDG Council in the development of Annual SDG Framework Report which was later submitted to the BIH Council of Ministers. The revised SDG indicators were adopted and National Perception survey on safety, integrity, public services and local transport is conducted.
The support was also provided to Parliamentary Assembly of BiH in following areas: Respective rulebook on procedure was amended to include sustainability, 1st Workshop on Sustainability for parliamentarians was organized aimed at familiarizing them with SDGs and procedures required to facilitate their integration. On the level of Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina social data monitoring database was developed. The database is currently pending publication. FBIH authorities also received support in developing Law on Social Services. Republika Srpska received support in development of RS Development Strategy 2030. On the BIH level under the component implemented by UN Women, "Gerentodomacice" (this term is used for women who are engaged in activities of providing care for people in need i.e elderly, persons with disabilities) and Entrepreneurs in Care more than 240 women received training.
In terms of unexpected results under this component the extent of technical support provided for developing a public interactive data visualization platform and the Councils active international engagement surpassed typical expectations. These activities not only enhanced domestic accountability but also improved BiHs visibility in global SDG dialogues. The integration of care work into economic planning also marked a unique institutional shift in BiH's policy framework.
The main result during this reporting period was an adoption of the SDG Financing Framework (SDG FF) by all government levels and SDG Bonds feasibility studies for Strategic Investment Fund are launched. In relation to public financing instruments 3 innovative financing mechanisms are piloted: 1) SME competitiveness grant scheme in Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina, 2) Digital transition scheme for local governments in Federation of BiH and Republika Srpska, 3) In Federation of BIH joint Research and Development grant scheme with academia and private sector.
The rapid development and scaling interest in the digital grant management platform, including cross-ministerial uptake, indicated unexpected momentum toward modernizing public financial management and be considered as unexpected result. Similarly, the substantive involvement of academic institutions and the quality of research outputs under the R&D Grant Scheme showed a stronger-than-anticipated capacity in the science and innovation sectors.
This year program traditionally organized SDG Business Pioneers Awards, promoting ESG and circular economy practices and supported organization of SDG Week. This year it increased private sector awareness and participation (e.g., 484 companies in 2025) reflected the project's sustained influence. The Circular Economy Accelerator was launched and it helped 10 SMEs to develop their transition plans. Green Transition Web Platform is used by over 50 companies.
Within the output where UNDP cooperates closely with UNICEF, in the reporting period the program succeeded in integrated SDGs into planning & reporting of 6 local communities in Bosnia and Herzegovina and 2 local communities adopted development strategies. These local communities as reported previously were selected on the basis of an open call applying earlier agreed methodology for eligibility. 8 local communities are in the process of developing documentation for large infrastructure project documentation.
Most importantly 9 local communities through SDG localization grant projects implemented (BAM 1.3M total value, LGs co-financing BAM 326,498 - 25%. There are 3,014 direct beneficiaries of these projects out of which 49% are women & 61% are children and youth. 43,283 are considered as indirect beneficiaries. The program helped support 7 new & 3 improved social services available with local communities. Social Protection and Inclusion (SPI) Commissions & Operational Teams are established in 7 Local governments to facilitate provision of new and improved services. For example Novo Sarajevo formed a multi-sectoral working group for integrating youth with disabilities into the labor market.
The program also supported launching of 2025-2026 Local Action Plans by 8 governments and nearly 400 professionals from social and education sectors received training.
The success in co-financing (34%) from local authorities for Leave No One Behind projects demonstrated unexpected ownership and buy-in. The establishment of SPI Commissions and development of multi-sectoral working groups (e.g., for youth with disabilities) revealed strong local commitment and innovation in cross-sectoral service delivery.
Further in Una-Sana and Tuzla cantons SDG aligned plans are developed, 3 strategic infrastructure proposals are finalized and 2 feasibility studies produced in Tuzla and West Herzegovina cantons.
5 grant funded projects are launched in total value of 843,900 whereby cantons are co-financing 48% of total value (404,746). Nearly 18 000 persons are direct beneficiaries of these projects out of which 42,3% are women.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
